source_text: 22 DE UBIQUE PARATIS. Dum uentri seruis, innocentem esse te dicis, Et quasi communis facis te ubique paratum. Uae tibi, stulte homo, mortem circumspicis ipse, Barbaro de more sine lege uiuere quaeris: Ipse tibi figis asciam in crure de uerbo. Qui simplicem fingis, simpliciter uiue cum isto. Uiuere te credis, dum uentrem cupis implere. Exiguus tua in domo resedes, praue, Paratus ad epulas, et refugis cenae praecepta. Aut quia discredis Deum iudicare defunctos, Rectorem caeli facis te tu forte pro illo? Aspicis ad uentrem, quasi tu sis prouidus illi. Tu modo profanus, modo sanctus esse uideris. In supplicem prodis Dei sub aspectu, tyranne. Senties in fatis, cuias modo legem inanis.
pass_a_gloss: Ventri seruis → innocentem fingis. Sine lege. Cenae praecepta refugis. Si discredis Deum iudicare defunctos — Rectorem caeli te? Profanus/sanctus. Senties in fatis.
pass_b_english: While you serve the belly you say you are innocent, and as if common you make yourself ready everywhere. Woe to you, foolish man — you yourself look round at death; in barbarian fashion you seek to live without law: you yourself plant an axe in your shin by the word. You who feign the simple — live simply with him. You believe you live while you long to fill the belly. Tiny, you sit back in your house, crooked one, ready for feasts, and you flee the dinner’s precepts. Or because you disbelieve that God judges the dead, do you happen to make yourself Rector of heaven in his place? You look to the belly as if you were provident for it. Now you seem profane, now holy. You come forth against the suppliant under God’s sight, tyrant. You will feel in the fates whose law you now empty.

choices.why: Deum iudicare defunctos; Rectorem caeli facis te

choices.reject: feign innocence while serving the belly

notes: Belly vs judgment of the dead.
